name: MEV Bot 0xd61492
rootCause: The MEV bot at address 0x8db0efee6a7622cd9f46a2cf1aedc8505341a1a7 on Arbitrum exposed a public entry-point function (0x0582f20f) that first borrowed funds from a companion Vault contract (0xd614927acfb9744441180c2525faf4cedb70207f) via flash loan, then executed arbitrage logic through a delegatecall to an external contract address supplied directly in the caller's calldata — with no validation whatsoever on that address. An attacker passed a malicious contract address as the delegatecall target, causing the arbitrage bot to execute attacker-controlled code in the context of the bot itself (with access to its funds and storage). This allowed the attacker to drain approximately $800K from the vault/bot system. The irony is notable: a bot designed to extract value from others was itself drained through a single missing input-validation check on a delegatecall target. Attack Tx: 0x864c8cfb8c54d3439613e6bd0d81a5ea2c5d0ad25c9af11afd190e5ea4dcfc1f Analysis: MEV Bot 0xd61492: From Predator to Prey (BlockSec)
